subject: software_engineering

resources.title: Software Engineering - LL EduCATE: Introduction to Engineering Concepts
resources.notes: High-school/non-credit introduction to software engineering, lifecycle, programming, testing, tooling, architecture, DevOps and common specializations. Mappings use exact canonical taxonomy keys.

resources.title: Pro Git, 2nd Edition
resources.notes: Official freely available Git book covering version control from fundamentals through advanced workflows; no longer overmapped to software_architecture.

resources.title: Software Construction
resources.notes: Software construction course focused on specifications, invariants, testing, abstract data types, design patterns, concurrency, functional programming, version control and team development. Only exact canonical taxonomy keys are mapped.

resources.title: Elements of Software Construction
resources.notes: Covers abstractions, modularity, interfaces, design patterns, invariants, testing and coverage, concurrency, usability, relational databases and team projects. Invalid non-taxonomy concurrency mapping removed.

resources.title: Laboratory in Software Engineering
resources.notes: Large-software-system engineering through modularity, specifications, data abstraction, object modeling, design patterns, testing and individual/group projects.

resources.title: Introduction to Algorithms
resources.notes: Data structures, sorting, graph search, dynamic programming, and performance analysis.

resources.title: Operating System Engineering
resources.notes: OS design and implementation using xv6 and RISC-V. Invalid non-taxonomy concurrency mapping removed.

resources.title: Operating System Engineering
resources.notes: Graduate systems course emphasizing UNIX, research papers, labs, and OS implementation. Invalid non-taxonomy concurrency mapping removed.

resources.title: Database Systems
resources.notes: Modern assessed database-systems course covering relational models, schema normalization, query processing and optimization, transactions and advanced systems topics. Includes labs, projects, assignments, exams and solutions.

resources.title: Distributed Computer Systems Engineering
resources.notes: Engineering course on distributed-system abstractions and implementation, including server design, network programming, naming, storage, security and fault tolerance, with labs, exams and projects.

resources.title: Computer Systems Security
resources.notes: Assessed systems-security course covering threat models, OS security, capabilities, information-flow control, language security, network protocols, hardware security and web security, with labs, exams and a final project.

resources.title: Computer Networks
resources.notes: Graduate network-systems course on Internet architecture, routing, congestion control, QoS, mobile networking, router architecture, network-aware applications, content dissemination, security and performance.

resources.title: arXiv Computer Science
resources.notes: Research/preprint discovery layer for computer science and software systems; individual papers require quality, version and rights verification and this portal alone does not establish expert readiness.

known_gaps: Graduate and research software engineering still needs stronger exact-cell primary literature beyond the general arXiv discovery layer.
Dedicated API design, cloud computing, site reliability engineering, compiler and ML-engineering curricula remain priority gaps where exact taxonomy cells are uncovered.
Foundation/beginner coverage for databases, networks, operating systems and security remains thinner than advanced university coverage.
Expert readiness still requires runtime retrieval, build projects, testing evidence, provenance and assessment rather than catalog coverage alone.
